items.stem: Complete the statement: When an account is balanced, the balance carried down (c/d) is entered on …
options: the side with the smaller total, then brought down on the opposite side
the side with the larger total
items.answer: the side with the smaller total, then brought down on the opposite side
items.markingKey: the side with the smaller total, then brought down on the opposite side. Balance c/d makes both sides equal; b/d goes to the larger side [1]

items.stem: Explain what a credit balance on the bank account in the ledger means.
items.answer: Payments out have exceeded receipts, so the business owes the bank money – it has an overdraft, a current liability.
items.markingKey: Payments > receipts [1]; overdraft/current liability [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why balance c/d and balance b/d are entered on opposite sides of an account.
items.answer: The c/d figure is inserted on the smaller side to make the totals agree; it is then brought down on the other side to show the true balance at the start of the next period.
items.markingKey: c/d equalises totals [1]; b/d shows opening balance on correct side [1] [2]

items.stem: Complete the statement: A trial balance is …

items.markingKey: a list of the balances on the ledger accounts at a date, in debit and credit columns. It is a list, not an account [1]

items.stem: State two purposes of preparing a trial balance.
items.answer: To check the arithmetical accuracy of the double entry (total debits = total credits); to provide a summary of balances from which financial statements are prepared.
items.markingKey: Arithmetical check [1]; basis for financial statements [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why drawings appear in the debit column of a trial balance.
items.answer: Drawings reduce the owner's capital (a credit balance), so the drawings account has a debit balance.
items.markingKey: Reduce capital [1]; therefore debit balance [1] [2]

items.stem: Which error would NOT be revealed by a trial balance?

An expense was posted to only one account
items.answer: Goods sold on credit to Ali were debited to Alia's account
items.markingKey: Goods sold on credit to Ali were debited to Alia's account. Error of commission – debits still equal credits [1]

items.stem: Explain why an error of commission is not revealed by the trial balance.
items.answer: The correct amount is debited and credited, but to the wrong account of the same class, so total debits still equal total credits.
items.markingKey: Correct amounts on both sides [1]; wrong account of same type, totals unaffected [1] [2]

items.stem: Distinguish between an error of principle and an error of commission.
items.answer: Principle: posted to the wrong class of account (e.g. asset as expense); commission: posted to the wrong account of the correct class (e.g. wrong customer).
items.markingKey: Principle – wrong class [1]; commission – right class, wrong account [1] [2]
